title: Confession and Witness
premise: Coral Quintana, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent years listening to strangers' last calls, recognizes the voice of a man reporting his own murder minutes before a body surfaces in the harbor — wearing her late brother's jacket, stolen from her closet. The victim, a retired cop turned informant, left behind a ledger of payoffs disguised as taxi fare records, and Coral realizes the killer is someone inside the dispatch office. As the tide threatens to wash away the evidence and the detective on the case suspects her of staging it all, Coral must decide whether to trust the ragtag crew of drivers she's come to call family. In the end, she decodes the ledger during one final shift, exposes the corrupt dispatcher who killed to bury it, and chooses to keep the found family that finally gave her a place to belong.
about_author: Dominic Brightwater is the pen name of a former harbor-town paramedic who spent a decade listening to radio traffic before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who do the right thing through the wrong doors.

chapters.title: The Call Before the Body
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. During a slow night shift, Coral takes a garbled call from a man whispering fare numbers before the line cuts; hours later, police arrive because a body pulled from the harbor wears clothes matching her own closet, including her dead brother's jacket. Detective Ibarra treats her as a suspect. Emotional beat: dread and uncanny recognition — the listener becomes the listened-to.

chapters.title: Fares and False Names
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Searching the victim's effects with help from driver Marisol and mechanic Teo, Coral finds a ledger of taxi fares that don't match any real routes — coded payments naming cops, clerks, and one dispatcher. Someone ransacks her apartment for the missing pages. Emotional beat: wary belonging as her makeshift family closes ranks around her.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. The tide gives up the victim's satchel with the final ledger page, but Ibarra arrests Teo on planted evidence, and Coral realizes the killer — dispatcher Ray Voss, protecting years of payoffs — is monitoring every call she makes. She sets a trap using the dispatch board itself, broadcasting coded fares only Voss would understand. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Confession at Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. At dawn, Voss comes to silence her, and Coral plays back his own recorded confession over the dispatch channel while Marisol stalls him and Ibarra, tipped by the broadcast, arrives to make the arrest. Teo is freed, the ledger goes public, and Coral keeps the brother's jacket, no longer a relic but an inheritance. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging.
